title: Sometimes the Model doth preach: Quantifying Religious Bias in Open LLMs through Demographic Analysis in Asian Nations
findings: Most open LLMs tested converge on a single, homogeneous demographic profile within each country, with little variation across different models. For instance, in India, models align with married Hindu males aged 35-44 from rural Northern India. This uniformity raises concerns about LLMs promoting a hegemonic worldview. Furthermore, the study found that zero-shot steering prompts, intended to make the model adopt a specific religious persona, were ineffective at significantly altering the models' underlying opinions.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the demographic profile, including religious identity and tolerance, reflected in the opinions of Large Language Models. It achieves this by comparing LLM responses to survey questions with the responses of actual human survey participants in various Asian nations, using Hamming Distance to find the closest matching demographic group.
